statement: I checked Herrmann's open arXiv v2, sections 2–3 and Appendices A–C. The abstract disclaims a translation of the manuscript as a whole. The catalogue phrase that the author explicitly refrains from translation needs that scope. Section 3.4 gives an explicitly word-by-word gloss for a short sequence on f77v. Appendix C proposes a translation of much of the f116v colophon and labels it highly speculative. Section 2 also separates six direct reversals from two matches involving a diacritic and three further matches requiring other rotations or reflection, for a total of eleven claimed similarities. Appendix B uses different treatments of leading o in different words, and explicitly marks inserted and ignored characters. Appendix A drops initial signs in two tentative matches. These are documented editorial choices affecting whether Tables 1–2 can be frozen as a deterministic manuscript-wide key. The catalogue's broader description of the alphabet hypothesis and selected lexical examples agrees with the paper.
